_comment: Gold cases for app.services.retrieval.fuse_rrf(), the pure RRF arithmetic extracted from HybridRetriever.retrieve(). This is the only offline-testable slice of real ranking logic in retrieval.py -- vector/lexical search themselves are raw SQL against a live Postgres and have no offline path (see test_gold_retrieval_offline.py's module docstring for why full paraphrase-quality Recall@k needs a DATABASE_URL-gated e2e companion instead). Each case supplies pre-computed semantic_hits/lexical_hits, exactly the shape _vector_search/_lexical_search return -- [id, table, rank] triples, rank is 0-based position within that one signal's own ranking.

cases.notes: Both signals rank the same doc first -- RRF must not let a lower-ranked doc in either list overtake it.

Represents a paraphrased query ('debug intermittent auth failures' for a procedure literally titled 'fix flaky authentication tests'): the lexical (keyword) signal finds nothing relevant because the wording doesn't overlap, but the semantic signal alone must still be enough for RRF to surface the right doc. This is a real production-code check of fuse_rrf's behavior under a semantic-only hit; it does NOT test whether the embedding model itself would actually produce that semantic_hits ranking for real paraphrased text -- that requires a live embedder + DB, tracked as a documented gap, not faked here.
A very short query ('restart worker') typically returns few hits per signal -- RRF must still work correctly with single-element ranked lists, not just long ones.
A long, detailed query surfaces many candidates per signal -- docs appearing in BOTH lists (proc-a, proc-c) must fuse to the top even if neither signal alone ranked them #1.
'Clear the browser state' is genuinely ambiguous between two acceptable procedures -- the gold set accepts either, unlike the single-answer cases above. Recall@2 must reach both.

A query using terminology never seen in any procedure's stored text (e.g. slang for 'rotate the API key') produces zero lexical hits at all -- fuse_rrf must handle an empty ranked list for one signal without erroring or zeroing out the other signal's contribution.

Two procedures with near-identical wording from different repositories both surface in both signals -- at k=1 the fused ranking must not let the wrong-repository one win a tie/near-tie by accident (deterministic tie-break is a separate concern from this gold set; here relevant strictly outranks irrelevant in both raw signals, so RRF has no excuse to invert that).
